mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to decreased liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which often precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods following two consecutive GDPC1 declines, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals supply chain disruptions, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO drops and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, the combination signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in real personal savings (RSAFS) signals a shift in consumer spending from savings to real estate, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises and RSAFS falls in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in one month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is rising and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is falling, it signals a robust economic environment with strong supply and labor conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises and UNRATE falls in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of INDPRO and UNRATE on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
